title: Technical English — Course 4, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 14

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the signal lesson begin?
tasks.audioText: The instrumentation lecturer will discuss analogue and digital signals on Wednesday at one fifteen. Students should meet in Room 21 and bring the signal glossary. The lesson will compare a continuously varying signal with a signal represented by distinct states or values. Example diagrams will be provided for annotation during the session.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which instrumentation vocabulary resource should students bring?
tasks.audioText: The instrumentation lecturer will discuss analogue and digital signals on Wednesday at one fifteen. Students should meet in Room 21 and bring the signal glossary. The lesson will compare a continuously varying signal with a signal represented by distinct states or values. Example diagrams will be provided for annotation during the session.

tasks.prompt: An analogue signal can vary continuously over a range, while a digital signal is represented by distinct levels or values. A sensor system may convert a physical measurement into a signal that another device can process. The signal format, range and interface depend on the equipment design. A technical description should identify the relevant signal type and refer to the system documentation. Reading 1. How is a digital signal represented?
What should a technical description identify?
A digital signal ___ by distinct levels or values.
Choose TWO correct statements about signal types.
options: An analogue signal is always a printed label
A digital signal is a mechanical bearing
An analogue signal can vary continuously
A digital signal uses distinct levels or values

tasks.prompt: A signal that can vary continuously over a range is an ___ signal.
A signal type is not clear in a system description. What should you ask?
options: I will label it without checking.
Could we confirm the signal type in the system documentation?
The signal type is not important.
I will assume every signal is digital.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of electronic signal descriptions in a logical order.
options: Check the range and interface information
Identify the measured or controlled quantity
Describe the signal with reference to documentation
correctOrder: Identify the measured or controlled quantity
Check the range and interface information
Describe the signal with reference to documentation

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words comparing analogue and digital signals. Include one difference and explain why system documentation is needed.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: task completion and relevant content (0–2); clear organisation and logical linking (0–2); grammar and sentence structure (0–2); accurate electrical vocabulary, spelling and punctuation (0–2). Minor errors are acceptable if meaning remains clear.
